posts.title: How to choose the right fabric for your OEM backpack
posts.excerpt: 1000D Cordura, 900D Oxford, ripstop or canvas? A buyer-friendly guide to matching fabric to price, weight and durability.
posts.content:
Choosing fabric is the single biggest decision in a private-label bag project. It changes the price, the weight, the feel in the hand and how long the bag survives in the real world. Here is how we explain it to new buyers.

## 1000D Cordura nylon
The tactical favourite. It resists abrasion and tearing, which is why it is used for military-style packs and heavy duffels. It is heavier and costs more, so choose it when durability is the selling point.

## 900D Oxford and 600D polyester
A smart middle path. With a polyurethane coating it becomes water resistant, prints well and keeps the unit cost low. It suits school bags, gym duffels and promotional bags where the price per unit matters.

## Ripstop nylon
Light and strong. A reinforcing grid is woven into the cloth, so a small puncture does not spread. It is ideal for travel organizers, packing cubes and foldable bags.

## Waxed canvas and leather-look
These are about style. They age beautifully and photograph well, but they are heavier and need more care. Good for lifestyle and fashion brands.

## Our advice
Start from the use case and the target retail price, then pick the fabric. Send us your tech pack or a reference bag and we will suggest two or three fabric options with sample swatches before you commit to a full run.

posts.title: MOQ explained: how small can a custom bag order be?
posts.excerpt: Why factories ask for a minimum order quantity, and how to keep your first private-label run small and smart.
posts.content:
Every new buyer asks the same question: what is the minimum order? The honest answer is that it depends on the bag, the fabric and how much of it is custom.

## Why MOQ exists
Cutting patterns, setting up stitching lines and sourcing fabric all have a fixed cost. Spreading that cost over a few units makes each bag expensive. MOQ is the point where the price per unit becomes fair for both sides.

## Typical starting points at Bagzinic
Tactical backpacks and luggage usually start around 200 to 250 units per colourway. Lighter accessories and drawstring packs start at about 500 units. Branded details such as woven labels or laser-cut buckles can be added from the first run.

## How to keep the first order small
- Use stock fabrics and standard colours instead of custom-dyed cloth.
- Limit yourself to one or two colourways.
- Start with our existing patterns and customise colours, logo and hardware.
- Ask for a pilot run, then scale once the market responds.

## Next step
Use the 3D customizer on our website to design your bag, then send it to us. We will reply with a quotation that shows MOQ and price breaks.

posts.title: From tech pack to container: our production timeline
posts.excerpt: A simple walk-through of what happens after you send your design, and how long each stage normally takes.
posts.content:
Buyers often tell us that the unknown is what worries them most. So here is the path every order follows.

## 1. Tech pack review
You send a tech pack, a drawing or even a reference photo. Our engineers check materials, dimensions and stitching details and convert the bill of materials into cutting plots, normally within 72 hours.

## 2. Prototype
We make a sample so you can feel the fabric, test the zippers and check the fit. Our prototype delivery target is 30 days. Samples travel by courier from Sialkot.

## 3. Approval and deposit
Once you approve the sample and the deposit is agreed, we book fabric and hardware.

## 4. Production
Cutting, stitching, hardware assembly and quality checks run in parallel lines. As a guide, runs below 500 units take about 20 to 25 days, up to 2,000 units about 25 to 30 days, and larger runs 35 to 45 days.

## 5. Final inspection and shipping
Finished bags are inspected, packed into cartons and shipped FOB Karachi or CIF to your destination port. You receive photos before the container leaves.

Timelines depend on fabric availability and order size, and your quotation will state the dates for your project.

posts.title: Why Sialkot is a global hub for bags and sporting goods
posts.excerpt: A short look at the city behind Bagzinic: skills, supply chain and export experience.
posts.content:
Sialkot, in Pakistan's Punjab province, has been an export city for well over a century. It is best known for sporting goods, leather products and surgical instruments, and that experience matters for bag making too.

## Skilled people
Generations of workers have learned cutting, stitching and finishing here. That skill shows in details such as bar-tack reinforcement, clean seams and consistent zipper installation.

## A complete supply chain
Fabric, webbing, zippers, foam, printing and packaging suppliers are close by. A short supply chain means faster sampling and fewer delays when you change a colour or a component.

## Export know-how
Local factories are used to international compliance, packing standards and shipping documents. Sialkot also has its own international airport, which helps when you need prototypes fast.

## What this means for you
You get a partner who understands export orders and can move from sample to shipment efficiently. If you would like to see the factory first, you can book a live video tour from our About page.
